{"path": "app/models/topic_embed.rb", "line": 13, "severity": "Critical", "claim": "The 'Imported from' footer interpolates url unescaped into <a href='#{url}'>. Because the post is cooked raw_html, a single quote in an attacker-chosen embed_url injects an event-handler attribute, giving unauthenticated stored XSS on the forum origin.", "evidence": "Reachable from the unauthenticated embed_url param: EmbedController#best -> Jobs::RetrieveTopic -> TopicRetriever -> import_remote -> import. The only gates are a host-equality check (topic_retriever.rb:15) and a Referer check (embed_controller.rb:26), which a non-browser client forges. Ruby's RFC2396 URI parser accepts ' in the path and query. absolutize_urls (Nokogiri) turns the injected text into a real onmouseover attribute. Post#cook returns raw for raw_html (post.rb:133). Reasoned test from open-code-review: TopicEmbed.import(user, \"http://eviltrout.com/?a='onmouseover='alert(1)\", title, 'x') then post.cooked.should_not =~ /onmouseover/. Not executed.", "seats": ["open-code-review", "superpowers", "mattpocock"], "verdict": "fix", "reason": "Raised by 3 seats. Both correctness seats rate it Critical. The claim is reasoned only, so the open-code-review spec must be shown red on the pinned code before fixing. The fix is to escape url.", "list": "main"},
{"path": "app/models/post.rb", "line": 133, "severity": "Critical", "claim": "The raw_html cook method stores feed content and Readability output as cooked HTML with no sanitization. Whoever controls the feed or the fetched page can inject script into the forum origin.", "evidence": "post.rb:133 has `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. Imports use cook_method: raw_html (topic_embed.rb:22). Feed content only passes through CGI.unescapeHTML and scrub (poll_feed.rb:35). Readability keeps href/src with any scheme, including javascript: (topic_embed.rb:48-50). Cooked HTML is rendered with raw (best.html.erb:19) and in normal topic views. A MITM on an http:// feed URL also works. Reasoned test from open-code-review: import contents '<script>alert(1)</script>' and assert cooked has no <script>. Not executed.", "seats": ["open-code-review", "superpowers", "mattpocock"], "verdict": "fix", "reason": "Raised by 3 seats. Normalised to Critical following superpowers, which grades the feed path as part of its Critical finding; open-code-review rated it Important. Reasoned only, so a red test is needed before fixing. The fix is to sanitise raw_html content against a whitelist.", "list": "main"},
